results.summary:
I checked the yg check / --approve / lock area on all five surfaces against release/6.1.0 source and the live 6.1.0 CLI. The live runs used a scratch project, $TMPDIR/chk-a in the container (since deleted): no reviewer, then an unreachable ollama reviewer; auto_approve set to false, deterministic and full; CI=1; log_required types; a throwing check.mjs; a conflict-markered lock; a garbled deterministic cache; a held .yg-approve.lock.

Much of the area agrees with the implementation. That includes the verdict line format, block labels, the 12-member cap, --top/--summary/--details/--aspect refusals and tags, the dry-run exit-0/preview JSON, the ABORTED report and the aborted document, the cause list and its order, CI hold-back of auto_approve: full in the code, lock triad file names, empty-husk removal, derived-cache tolerance, the approve lock file and the 12h staleness, the 256/1 s flush figures, and the det contract 2.

The mismatches below are real and provable. Most serious:
- **Log gate:** described everywhere as "any drifted log_required node stops the whole fill". In the code it only gates components that own unverified pairs.
- **aspect-check-runtime-error:** documented as an issue code, but no issue carries that code.
- **Infrastructure failures:** after a check.mjs failure, next: and the JSON next point back at a bare, paid `yg check --approve` and drop the flags the user ran with.
- **Feature index:** `--approve` does write .feature-field.json, although two surfaces say it leaves it alone.
- **Committed writes:** `--only-deterministic` and auto_approve: deterministic write a committed aspect log.md, although they are described as touching no committed file.
- **CI hold-back:** the auto_approve: full hold-back under CI is missing from the-lock, prime, three knowledge topics and the config schema.

Many smaller wording and coverage gaps follow. Source root: Yggdrasil/source/cli/src.

kept.surfaces: docs:the-lock + prime (rules.ts Log management) + knowledge:log-management vs code/live CLI
kept.claim: The log gate is all-or-nothing: if ANY log_required node is missing its entry, --approve fills nothing at all, no pair on any node.
kept.evidence:
docs/the-lock.md:135: "at `--approve`, if *any* `log_required` node is missing its entry, the run fills **nothing at all** — no pair on any node, related or not."
Prime (templates/rules.ts:282-285): "if ANY `log_required` node's source drifted with no fresh entry, `--approve` fills NOTHING that run (no pair on any node is verified)".
knowledge log-management.ts:108-112: same wording.
Code core/fill-classify.ts:232-236: "The log gate's set: every component owning an unverified pair … for (const p of unverifiedPairs) nodeSet.add(p.nodePath)"; core/fill.ts:411-427 gates only nodeSet.
Live: type `lib` (log_required, no rules), source changed, no entry; svc2 pair unverified with entry. `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` printed "fill  1 pair · 1 script (free) … fill  done in 0s — 1 passed" then "yg check: FAIL  1 error … error[log-entry-missing] 1 node changed with no log entry  at: lib". The run was not ABORTED.
kept.truth: The gate only stops the fill when a component that owns an unverified pair (a pair this run would fill) lacks its entry. A drifted log_required component with no pairs to fill (a rule-less node, all rules draft) does not stop the fill. It only shows as a read-only log-entry-missing error in the post-fill report.
kept.fix: Either gate on every drifted log_required node, as documented, or reword the-lock, prime and log-management: the fill stops when any component it would fill owes an entry; other unlogged components block the report, not the fill.

v.reason: Reproduced live. With lib (log_required, no rules) left without an entry, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` still filled 2 script pairs and then reported error[log-entry-missing] at lib, with no ABORTED. fill-classify.ts:232-236 builds the gate set only from nodes that own unverified pairs. So the-lock.md:135 ('fills nothing at all — no pair on any node, related or not'), prime rules.ts:282-285 and the knowledge topic are all wrong for a drifted node that has no pairs. The practical impact is small because the report still goes red, so severity is lowered to minor.

kept.surfaces: docs:cli-reference (yg-check-json + --approve sections) + CHANGELOG vs live CLI (text next: and yg-check/1 next)
kept.claim: For infrastructure causes, next: and the JSON next name the real fix, never the command that just failed. A paid `yg check --approve` is only named with its full cost and 'ask the user to approve it first'.
kept.evidence:
docs/cli-reference.md:380-382: "The infrastructure causes are ones re-running the same command cannot clear, so their `next` names the real fix, and once no pair a fill can settle is left, `suggestedNext` and `next` point there rather than back at the command that just failed."
cli-reference.md (Next contract): "`yg check --approve` is named only with its full cost, and its text says `ask the user to approve it first`".
Live after `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` with a throwing check.mjs, text ends "next: yg check --approve". JSON next = {"command":["yg","check","--approve"],"text":"yg check --approve","requiresUser":false,…}, suggestedNext "yg check --approve".
Source: ast/runner.ts:235 and structure/runner.ts:181 `next: \`Fix the bug in check.mjs, then re-run: yg check --approve\``; blockAction extracts the embedded command.
kept.truth: For check-failed-to-run, the step is a bare re-run of `yg check --approve`. It drops the edit instruction, escalates a free --only-deterministic run to the full fill, and carries no cost or ask-the-user annotation (requiresUser false).
kept.fix: Make the check-failed-to-run next 'edit <check.mjs>' (the real fix), with the retry in then: carrying the invoked command. Or document the behaviour.

v.reason: Reproduced. After `--approve --only-deterministic` with a throwing check.mjs, the text says 'next: yg check --approve' and the JSON next is {command:[yg,check,--approve], requiresUser:false}, with no edit instruction and no cost or 'ask the user' text. docs/cli-reference.md:333 lists check-failed-to-run among the infrastructure causes, and l.379-381 says their next names the real fix, not the command that just failed. It also silently turns a free run into the full fill.

kept.surfaces: docs:cli-reference 'Silent structural-deviation index' + knowledge:cli-reference vs code/live CLI
kept.claim: Only the reporting read path maintains .yggdrasil/.feature-field.json; --approve, --dry-run and the internal fill re-checks leave it alone.
kept.evidence:
docs/cli-reference.md:754-756: "Only the reporting read path maintains it — `--approve`, `--dry-run`, and the internal fill re-checks leave it alone."
knowledge cli-reference.ts:224-225: "Only the reporting read path maintains it; `--approve`, `--dry-run`, and the internal fill re-checks leave it untouched."
Code cli/check.ts:573 passes `writeFeatureIndex: true` to runFill; core/fill.ts:583-591: "This IS the reporting path for `--approve`, so it maintains the silent feature-field index".
Live: `rm .yggdrasil/.feature-field.json; yg check --approve --only-deterministic -q` → file re-created ({"v":2,"generatedAt":"2026-09-25T20:30:15.211Z",…}). After a second rm, `--approve --dry-run` left it absent.
kept.truth: Plain `yg check` and `yg check --approve` (including --only-deterministic and auto_approve fills) both write the index. Only --dry-run and the internal re-checks leave it alone.
kept.fix: Change both surfaces to: 'plain yg check and yg check --approve maintain it; only --dry-run and internal re-checks leave it alone'.

v.reason: Reproduced. After rm .feature-field.json, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic -q` re-created it, and `--approve --dry-run` did not. fill.ts:583-591 says explicitly that this is the reporting path for --approve and that it maintains the index. docs/cli-reference.md:754-756 and the knowledge topic say --approve leaves it alone. The file is a gitignored index, so severity is lowered to minor.

kept.surfaces: docs:the-lock + docs:cli-reference + --help + knowledge:verification-and-lock/cli-reference vs code/live CLI
kept.claim: `--only-deterministic` (and auto_approve: deterministic) writes only the gitignored cache and no committed file. Only a full `yg check --approve` writes a hand-changed status into the rule's log.
kept.evidence:
docs/the-lock.md:87: "One consequence of writing no committed file: …"
docs/cli-reference.md (--only-deterministic): "writes **only** the gitignored `.yg-lock.deterministic.json` cache".
docs/cli-reference.md:1241-1244: "the next `yg check --approve` writes the bare fact into that rule's log".
configuration.md table: deterministic "writes the gitignored cache".
Live: auto_approve: deterministic, readable status edited by hand, bare `yg check` printed "fill  rule 'readable' now stands at draft (was enforced) — written into its own log"; `git status` → "?? .yggdrasil/aspects/readable/log.md" ("Status: enforced → draft, changed outside the CLI…").
Code core/fill.ts:536-540 calls recordAspectStatuses regardless of onlyDeterministic.
kept.truth: Any fill, including the free --only-deterministic CI step and a bare check under auto_approve: deterministic, appends a committed entry to .yggdrasil/aspects/<id>/log.md (or yg-aspect.adapt.log.md for package rules) when a rule's status moved by hand. Only the lock writes are scoped to the gitignored cache.
kept.fix: Say 'writes no committed LOCK file' and add that any fill (including --only-deterministic) records a hand-made status change in the rule's committed log. Or skip recordAspectStatuses under onlyDeterministic.

v.reason: Reproduced. After readable's status was edited by hand, `yg check --approve --only-deterministic` printed 'fill  rule 'readable' now stands at draft (was enforced) — written into its own log', and git status showed '?? .yggdrasil/aspects/readable/log.md' (and ' M' on a later run). This contradicts the-lock.md:83 ('without ever needing a key or touching a committed file') and the 'writes only the gitignored cache' wording in cli-reference, the help text and knowledge. That keyless, no-committed-write invariant is what the CI step is sold on.

kept.evidence:
docs/the-lock.md:7 and :73: "`auto_approve: full` behaves like `yg check --approve`. CI scripts use explicit flags … and are unaffected". No mention of the CI variable, yet docs/how-it-works.md:44 says "The mechanics, and the full `auto_approve` story, live in [The lock]".

kept.surfaces: docs:cli-reference (yg-check-json) vs yg-check/1 aborted document
kept.claim: `next.remaining` puts every error in exactly one bucket. In an aborted document the rest of the document is the read-only report of the same tree.
kept.evidence:
docs/cli-reference.md:370: "`remaining` puts every error in exactly one bucket by what clears it".
Live `yg check --approve --json` aborted by config-reviewer-missing: totals.errors = 5, while next.remaining = {needsFix:0, fillable:0, needsUser:1, waitingOnReviewer:0} (sum 1) and next.cost = {free:0, reviewerPairs:0}.
Code check-render-views.ts:626-636 builds remaining from the abort blocks only and hard-codes cost to zero.
kept.truth: In an aborted document, `next.remaining` covers only the gating findings and `cost` is always zero. The rest of the document (totals, issues) describes the whole tree.
kept.fix: Compute remaining from the full read-only blocks, or document that in an aborted document next/remaining describe only the gate.

v.reason: Reproduced. `yg check --approve --json` aborted on config-reviewer-missing with totals.errors 3 and 5 issues, while next.remaining summed to 1 (needsUser 1) and cost was zero. docs/cli-reference.md says remaining puts every error in exactly one bucket and that the rest of an aborted document is the read-only report of the tree.

kept.verifier: Reproduced. `yg check --approve --json` aborted on config-reviewer-missing with totals.errors 3 and 5 issues, while next.remaining summed to 1 (needsUser 1) and cost was zero. docs/cli-reference.md says remaining puts every error in exactly one bucket and that the rest of an aborted document is the read-only report of the tree.

results.summary:
I audited yg-config.yaml and yg-secrets.yaml, the reviewer providers, tiers, consensus, parallel, timeouts, keys and env vars, max_prompt_chars, prompt format, isolation, cost reporting, yg init (flags and interactive) and the threat model. I compared the five surfaces against source on release/6.1.0 (commit 65bfb3967) and against the live 6.1.0 CLI in scratch projects under $TMPDIR/cfgaudit-*. Those projects and the test servers have been removed.

Most parser claims hold: the 11 top-level keys, the three committed-only keys, and the tier regex. The reserved tier name `default`, the consensus odd-integer rule, the openai-compatible endpoint requirement and the model defaults (haiku, o4-mini, gemini-2.5-flash; copilot-cli has none) are also right. So are max_prompt_chars defaulting to 50000, the CLI tier defaults (parallel 4 written by init, timeout 300 s, API timeout 60 s), the env var names, the credential checks and the .gitignore list.

I found 26 mismatches, 12 of them major. The most serious are these:
- **Stale key sent to a new provider (proven live).** When `yg init --provider` switches provider, the old key stays in yg-secrets.yaml. The captured request showed an Anthropic key sent as a Bearer token to an openai-compatible endpoint, while init had printed that it would call the endpoint "without one".
- **Env key copied to disk.** Non-interactive init writes the key from the environment variable into yg-secrets.yaml, although the docs and the wizard say it is never copied.
- **Threat-model table wrong.** `--approve --only-deterministic` and `yg adopt` also run companion.mjs (proven live with a marker file).
- **Cold-companion impact claim wrong.** docs/the-lock.md and a knowledge topic say `yg impact --file` "runs the resolver" for companion rules with no verdict yet; the code does not.
- **Timeout said to be ignored.** The config schema says API providers ignore `timeout`; they honour it.
- **Hidden retry on timeout.** Hosted API calls silently retry once on a timeout or network error. That doubles the wall time and the requests, while the message still quotes the single timeout.
- **Wrong error code in a knowledge example.** The `consesnsus:` typo produces `config-tier-consensus-invalid`, not `config-tier-unknown-key` as the knowledge topic says.
- **`quality:` typos pass silently.** The docs call tier `config:` "the one exception" to unknown-key rejection, but `quality:` typos are ignored too.
- **debug claims wrong.** The debug log is only written by 12 commands, yet aspect-test and drill tell the user to set `debug: true`, which writes nothing for them.
- **CI rule missing from agent-facing text.** The 6.1.0 breaking change that holds `auto_approve: full` back under CI is absent from knowledge, schema and prime.
- **Comment-stripping claim false.** Docs say configuring a reviewer strips yg-config.yaml comments; it does not, and cli-reference contradicts itself on this.

The minor findings include:
- errors in yg-secrets.yaml blamed on yg-config.yaml
- the claim that an overlay "never invalidates baselines", which is false
- a false note about which variable the openai provider reads
- the copilot-cli "no tools" overclaim
- `yg simulate` and the portal Approve button missing from the threat model
- about 16 `config-*` error codes that no surface documents

kept.claim: Switching provider with `yg init --provider <new>` leaves the previous provider's key active while init says there is no key; 'A missing key is non-fatal ... can be fixed later by exporting the variable'.
kept.evidence: Live: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-test-FAKE123 yg init --provider anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5` wrote .yggdrasil/yg-secrets.yaml `reviewer.tiers.standard.config.api_key: sk-ant-test-FAKE123`. Then `yg init --provider openai-compatible --model m1 --endpoint http://localhost:9999/v1` printed "No API key found in $OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY; the reviewer will call http://localhost:9999/v1 without one." and `--provider openai` printed "wrote the config without one", but yg-secrets.yaml still held the anthropic key. A capture server behind an openai-compatible tier with such an overlay logged `{"url":"/v1/chat/completions","auth":"Bearer sk-ant-STALE-<fake, from the previous provider>"}`. Code: init.ts:331-336 calls writeSecretsFile only `if (apiKey)` and never clears the old one; writeReviewerConfig replaces only the committed reviewer section (init-reviewer-setup.ts:371-373); api-utils.ts:17-20 `if (config.api_key) return config.api_key;` before any env var. knowledge cli-reference.ts:1516-1518: "A missing key is non-fatal: the config is written anyway and can be fixed later by exporting the variable"; docs/configuration.md:211: openai-compatible "never reads OPENAI_API_KEY ... an OpenAI key must not travel to it".
kept.truth: The overlay's api_key for the bootstrap tier `standard` survives every provider switch and takes precedence over any env var. So the new provider receives the old provider's key. Exporting the new variable does not fix it, and init's message saying there is no key is false.
kept.fix: When --provider (or the wizard) rewrites the `standard` tier, remove or replace `reviewer.tiers.standard.config.api_key` in yg-secrets.yaml, or at least detect it and warn that it will be sent. Make the 'no key' message check the overlay. Document the precedence in knowledge and docs.

results.summary:
Graph-model area (nodes, yg-node.yaml, mapping, architecture types and when/parents/relations/log_required/enforce, coverage, flows, ports, dot-directory nodes, glossary terms): I checked it against the release/6.1.0 source and the live 6.1.0 CLI, using 9 scratch projects under $TMPDIR/graphmodel-* in the container.

There are 21 mismatches, 6 of them major:
- **Nodes silently not loaded.** A node under a model directory that has no yg-node.yaml is dropped from the graph without any finding. So is every child of a node whose yg-node.yaml fails to parse. `yg check` still reports PASS. Every surface says nodes nest by directory.
- **`yg impact --type` does not preview strict gaps.** The docs promise it previews strict orphans and misplaced files before you set `enforce: strict`. The CLI shows that section only after the flag is set. When it does show it, it gets it wrong: every file under a directory or glob mapping is listed as an orphan, and misplaced files are never found.
- **`file-mapping-gitignored` described wrongly.** nodes.md says it fires for a directly named file that is untracked. The code fires it for a gitignored file, tracked or not. An untracked file that is not ignored gets no error at all.
- **Unknown keys silently ignored.** yg-node.yaml and the top level of yg-architecture.yaml ignore unknown keys without a word. A node-level `log_required`, or a typo such as `aspect:`, is dropped. The architecture parser also silently drops a `parents:` or `aspects:` written as a single value instead of a list. This contradicts the architecture parser's own "reject typos loudly" rule for type entries.
- **One bad flow file stops every command.** A malformed or missing yg-flow.yaml, including an empty directory under flows/, aborts every command with an undocumented `graph-load-failed` error. A broken node file only produces a per-node finding.
- **`yg impact` under-reports flows.** It ignores the documented rule that a flow includes the descendants of its participants: `impact --node` says "Flows: (none)" for a node that `yg context` shows as a participant.

The minor findings:
- **Globs.** Mapping entries and coverage roots are called minimatch globs, but only `*` switches glob matching on. `{a,b}`, `?` and `[]` are taken literally, while the same pattern does work in `when.path`.
- **`parents:` not checked at the top level.** It is never checked for top-level nodes, and no surface says so.
- **Hidden findings.** An architecture-level error (for example `enforce-strict-without-when`) hides all per-node findings until it is fixed.
- **Identical mappings.** Parent and child mapping the same entry give an undocumented `file-duplicate-mapping` error. There is no child-wins rule for this case.
- **Undocumented codes.** More than ten graph error codes appear on no surface at all.
- **Wording errors.** Schema, knowledge, showcase and glossary have wording errors about `port-names-empty`, de-duplication of strict findings, "always effective" bare attachments, `has_port` and a non-existent `node_type:` atom, the type-covered definition, and what the lock records for a node with no aspects.
- **Smaller gaps.** The `consumes` field name in yg-node/1, the config schema's coverage comments, the init architecture template, and the content-atom size limits.

Relevant source: Yggdrasil/source/cli/src/core/graph-loader.ts, io/node-parser.ts, io/architecture-parser.ts, io/flow-parser.ts, core/validator.ts, core/checks/{architecture,mapping,relations}.ts, cli/impact.ts, cli/impact-handlers.ts, utils/mapping-path.ts. Docs: Yggdrasil/docs/{nodes,relations-flows-ports,glossary,showcase,cli-reference,configuration}.md.

results.summary:
I audited the relations area across the five surfaces, checking each claim against code and live scratch runs in the container (CLI 6.1.0). The surfaces covered were docs/relations-flows-ports.md (including Known grammar limits), the ports-and-relations and verification-and-lock knowledge topics, the prime sections on relations, the node and architecture schemas, the cli-reference code table, getting-started, the CHANGELOG [6.1.0] relation entries, and the reference/relations palette. Confirmed as true: the verifier rules (ancestor/descendant exemption, a relation to a parent sanctions its subtree, one-directional), the SCC cycle report and self-loop, yg context blocking only the members a context draws on, the grammar pins in language-registry.ts against the docs table (every listed ERROR case reproduced against the shipped wasm), grammar:<lang> observations with the keyed-by-earlier-release cause, TS type-only and import defer edges, the C/C++ include roots and PHP composer rules, and event-unpaired matching by path.

Found 17 mismatches, four of them major:
- **Relation findings vanish on an invalid lock.** When a committed lock file is invalid, relation-undeclared-dependency, type-relation-forbidden and relation-parse-failed are all dropped. The 'partial:' banner still says the remaining findings were computed.
- **Relation type is ignored.** Any declared relation type sanctions a static import, including emits and listens, which the surfaces present as the cycle-free way to model two-way links. No surface says so, so an undeclared-dependency error can be silenced by adding an event-relation pair.
- **"Declaring relations re-opens nothing" is false.** A script rule that reads ctx.graph goes stale once a relation is declared (reproduced live).
- **JSON loses `edges` in progressive mode.** yg-check/1 omits `edges` on relation-undeclared-dependency-outside.

The minor ones:
- The grammar-limits text contradicts the ERROR-region rescan.
- The docs claim the build layout matters for only 2 languages, and the docs page is silent on the Python, Go, Rust, C# and Ruby rules.
- Knowledge and prime say "from scratch / not cached", but a parse cache exists.
- Several relation codes are documented nowhere.
- yg-node/1 emits `event_name` on structural relations.
- The node schema presents port-names-empty as a separate error code.
- The grammar table has no Rust row or JS import defer entry.
- The relation-parse-failed wording is wrong for a single-file parser failure.
- `edges.target` has two undocumented meanings.
- The changelog understates when yg context refuses.
- The docs call the check free of false positives by design, while the changelog lists false edges fixed in 6.1.0.
- getting-started overstates the no-cycle rule.
- The TS baseUrl fallback is described imprecisely.

results.summary:
Area: aspects and rules. I checked yg-aspect.yaml, reviewer vs script rules, the ctx API, companions, statuses and channels, implies, references, yg-suppress, drills, aspect-test, yg aspects (plus --health and --reach), aspect logs, and the yg-aspects/1, yg-aspects-health/1, yg-aspect-log/1, yg-drill/1 and yg-suppressions/1 documents. I compared every surface against source (release/6.1.0) and against live 6.1.0 runs in the dev container, in the scratch project $TMPDIR/aspaudit-1. I found 36 mismatches: 10 major and 26 minor.

Worst, confirmed live:
1. `yg drill add` of a .md file prints "behaves as expected" and exits 0. The rule's log says the rule does NOT refuse the case. `yg drill` then never runs that case.
2. A yg-suppress marker with no reason reaches much further than the docs say. For a script rule, one violation from any rule anywhere in that file leaves the pair unverified, whichever rule the marker names, even a nonexistent one. For a reviewer rule, prompt assembly fails even with no violation at all.
3. The knowledge topic says `yg aspects --health --json` is refused. The CLI emits yg-aspects-health/1, which Horde consumes.
4. The knowledge topic says rule-log read has only `--limit` and node-log read has no `--json`. Both are false.
5. `aspect-test --check-determinism` on a reviewer rule is not refused. It goes on to a live, paid reviewer call.
6. The status-drift warning still fires after the change was recorded, and its fix tells you to run a command that is now refused.
7. The aspect schema claims every .md file reaches the reviewer. Only content.md does; the others are only hashed.
8. The aspect schema recommends ctx.config for script rules. A local rule's `config:` is refused; only package rules have settings, and the schema never documents the key.
9. The knowledge topics disagree about what ctx drill and `aspect-test --files` supply.
10. A rule placed under any directory named `drills` is silently not loaded.

The minor findings are stale wording across prime, knowledge, docs and --help: trailing markers, the missing-reason warning, health-table column names, runner error codes, the parseAst language argument (ignored), the hash-contract list, the time budget, JSON range semantics, and error text that points at a file only Yggdrasil's own repo has.

kept.surfaces: docs:cli-reference#yg-drill-add + knowledge:cli-reference (drill add) + prime (drill add row) vs code (cli/drill-add.ts + core/drill-runner.ts discoverDrillCases)
kept.claim: drill add 'runs the rule over it and tells you what happened'; 'A rule that does not catch its own escape exits non-zero'; 'A case that turns out to be unmeasurable ... is taken back out'
kept.evidence: Live: `yg drill add --aspect no-b --violates src/notes.md@HEAD --why 'md escape'` -> stdout 'The rule 'no-b' behaves as expected on the new case. Recorded in the rule's log.' EXIT=0, while the log.md entry it wrote says 'The rule does NOT refuse it: the case is in the corpus as a standing record of a hole the rule still has.' A following `yg drill --aspect no-b` lists 3 cases and never the new violates-notes-20260925-3ddae41 case. Code: core/drill-runner.ts discoverDrillCases skips `if (baseName.toLowerCase().endsWith('.md')) continue;` and `yg-aspect.yaml`; cli/drill-add.ts:195-199 filters the discovered cases (now empty), `missed` is empty so it prints the success line, and caseLogEntry(caught=false) writes 'does NOT refuse'.
kept.truth: A drill-add of a .md file (or of a file named yg-aspect.yaml) writes a case that discovery can never see. Nothing is measured. The command reports success and exit 0 and records a contradictory log entry, and the case stays in the corpus forever, unmeasured.
kept.fix: Refuse such paths up front in drill add, or treat a zero-case measurement as unmeasurable: undo the write and exit non-zero. Document that .md and yg-aspect.yaml are never cases.

kept.surfaces: docs:cli-reference (suppress-marker-missing-reason row l.852, yg suppressions 'No reason'), docs:reviewers.md:599, yg suppressions warning text, knowledge:suppress-syntax vs code (structure/runner.ts rangesFor, structure/suppress-ranges.ts, core/verify-lock.ts, core/review-package.ts)
kept.claim: 'It waives nothing: the first violation in its range makes the fill reject it and leave the pair unverified' / 'once the check flags a line in its range, the fill fails that pair'
kept.evidence: Code: structure/runner.ts rangesFor(filePath) runs collectSuppressions over the WHOLE file the first time any violation lands in that file, and collectSuppressions throws SuppressMarkerError on any reasonless marker, whichever aspect it names. suppress-ranges.ts resolveSuppressedRangesForPrompt does the same for every reviewer pair's subjects, independent of violations. Live: `// yg-suppress(zzz)` (a nonexistent aspect, no reason) in src/b.ts -> `check --approve --only-deterministic`: 'warning: 4 pairs left unverified by a malformed yg-suppress marker', and cfg-local, nodesc, unknown-key and no-b are all unverified. Live: a reasonless `yg-suppress(no-b)` in src/a.ts made `aspect-test --aspect extra-md --node app --dry-run` fail with 'A yg-suppress marker at src/a.ts:2 (subject of aspect 'extra-md') is missing its required reason'.
kept.truth: A reasonless marker poisons its whole file: every script rule with any violation anywhere in that file, for every aspect, stays unverified. For reviewer rules the pair fails closed unconditionally, with no violation needed, whichever aspect the marker names.
kept.fix: Either scope the failure to the marker's own aspect and range, or document the real blast radius (whole file, all rules; reviewer pairs fail immediately) in cli-reference, reviewers.md, suppress-syntax and the warning text.

kept.surfaces: docs:aspects.md ('A rule keeps its own history') + docs/knowledge cli-reference (aspects log) vs code core/check-aspect-status.ts + core/log/aspect-status.ts findStatusDrift
kept.claim: docs/aspects.md:76: 'If you move a rule and record nothing, `yg check` says so'; knowledge: 'A change already recorded by the caller is never written twice.'
kept.evidence: Live: set no-b to status: advisory, then `yg aspects log add --aspect no-b --status advisory --evidence noisy --reason ...` succeeded. The next `yg check` still printed 'warning[aspect-status-changed-outside-cli] Rule 'no-b' now stands at advisory; the last status recorded for it was enforced ... this one moved without a word about why ... fix: Record why it moved: yg aspects log add --aspect no-b --status advisory ...'. Re-running that command is refused ('already stood at advisory'). findStatusDrift compares only the local memory in the gitignored .yg-lock.deterministic.json against the file and never reads the rule's log.
kept.truth: The warning fires whenever the local memory differs from the file, recorded or not, until the next full --approve. Because the memory is per-checkout, every teammate's machine warns 'moved without a word' even when the log holds the reason.
kept.fix: Make classifyAspectStatusDrift skip drift whose target already matches the log's last recorded status (as recordAspectStatuses does), or reword the warning and fix and document the local-memory semantics.

Lowered to minor because it is a non-blocking warning.

results.summary:
I audited the packages and marketplaces area across all five surfaces: docs/packages.md, the docs/cli-reference.md sections for `yg pack` and `yg marketplace`, docs/family-contracts.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/aspects.md, CHANGELOG [6.1.0], the knowledge topics packages-and-marketplaces and cli-reference, `yg prime` and its package notice, `yg schemas`, and the `--help` of every pack and marketplace subcommand. I checked them against the source (cli/pack*.ts, cli/marketplace.ts, core/marketplace-check.ts, core/checks/packages.ts, io/package-*.ts, io/aspect-adapt-parser.ts, the graph loader, check-render-views.ts) and against the live 6.1.0 CLI, using scratch marketplace and consumer repos under $TMPDIR/pkaudit-* in the container.

Most documented behaviour holds up. It all matched the code: pinning, `--to latest`, downgrade refusal, all-or-nothing update, the untagged-source sweep that exits 1, the tag/commit backfill for 6.0.0 records, moved-tag and re-used-number handling, `--reinstall --accept-republished`, the identity re-check on update, the command lock, the credential-free record, the versions cache, the reserved `packages/` directory, drill-add refusal and the adapt log placement.

The serious mismatches:
1. `yg marketplace check` says "Ready to publish" (exit 0) for packages that every consumer install refuses: the three version numbers disagree, `requires.yg` cannot be satisfied, the package contains a symlink, a binary file or a node_modules directory. The knowledge topic's publishing steps also imply the check catches version disagreement.
2. For `package-file-modified`, the `next:` step of `yg check` (and `next.command` in yg-check/1) is cut down to a bare `yg pack update`. That exact command is refused on an edited copy.
3. The docs say `update` describes each rule's changes "before it swaps anything in". The CLI prints that description after the swap.
4. The docs say `yg pack add` refuses when a rule with the same name already exists. In practice it overwrites and deletes a repository's own rule sitting at that install path.
5. `yg pack list` says "copy untouched" and `yg pack verify` says "exactly … (exit 0)" while `yg check` blocks on an unrecorded file in the copy. Files whose names start with a dot are never checked at all, although the docs say every unrecorded file blocks.
6. The command that `list` and `advise` suggest for a newer version (`--to <newest>`) silently pins a package that was set to follow the newest version.

There are also many smaller gaps and contradictions: the attention-item vs nomination naming, codes and features no reference page mentions, a nonexistent `yg marketplace new` in the CHANGELOG, a stale `yg prime` notice, the adapt stub's list of keys you cannot adapt, and remediation messages that cannot work.

The knowledge topic's "Updating a package you publish" says: "2. Raise version: in yg-package.yaml AND the entry in yg-marketplace.yaml … A consumer is refused a version whose tag, package manifest and marketplace entry disagree. 3. `yg marketplace check`."

The consumer then got `error: The package 'house-style' needs a Yggdrasil matching 'banana'` and, once that was fixed, `The version of 'house-style' is written down three ways that disagree`. A package holding `node_modules/` → check `Ready to publish`, but install refused with `carries a directory 'node_modules' that aspects: does not declare` (marketplace-check.ts:247 filters `node_modules`; pack-source readPackage/listPackageAspectDirs does not). results.summary:
Logs and history area of Yggdrasil 6.1.0 (release/6.1.0, live CLI 6.1.0), audited across all five surfaces. I read these sources: cli/log.ts, core/log/{log-add,log-read,log-entry,log-gate,log-merge-resolve}.ts, core/log-format.ts, core/log-integrity.ts, core/check-log-state.ts, core/fill.ts, core/fill-classify.ts, core/fill-closure.ts, core/fill-log-gate.ts, io/log-store.ts, io/lock-store.ts, io/atomic-write.ts, portal/server/{approve,router}.ts and cli/output.ts. I compared them against knowledge log-management, verification-and-lock and cli-reference.ts; prime (rules.ts); the docs pages cli-reference, the-lock, concurrency, progressive-mode, nodes, glossary and family-contracts; CHANGELOG [6.1.0]; the architecture schema; and --help for log, log add, log read and log merge-resolve. Behaviour was checked in scratch projects under $TMPDIR/yglog-* in the dev container.

Most claims hold. These were confirmed live: yg-log/1 fields; default --top 10; --top and --all are mutually exclusive; the text and JSON forms of --with-verdicts; the refusals of ## headers and unbalanced fences; timestamps that only move forward; CRLF-normalised integrity; the log-conflict routing; merge-resolve at a merge stop, at a rebase stop, on the merge commit, with --ours/--theirs and below the git root; the next: line after merge-resolve; the 10 s .yg-log.lock wait; the .yg-approve.lock refusal; and the dry-run log-gate preview.

Proven mismatches:
- Three are major and concern behaviour:
  - (a) The documented "all-or-nothing" log gate is not all-or-nothing. A log_required node that owes an entry but owns no unverified pair does not stop --approve.
  - (b) A conflict-markered log.md does not stop --approve. --approve then writes a new committed source fingerprint over it, yet the surfaces call log-conflict a gate prerequisite.
  - (c) merge-resolve advances only the log baseline. After the documented merge recipe, a log_required node therefore owes a new entry, and no surface says so.
- One is major and concerns an agent-facing surface: knowledge cli-reference, and a table in the docs cli-reference, deny that `yg log read --json` exists.
- The rest are minor: wrong message texts; missing error codes in the reference tables; error codes that differ from the documented grammar; log-cycle-open firing in the ordinary workflow; progressive mode demoting malformed logs to warnings; the typo-recovery window; the take-a-side lock recipe for yg-lock.logs.json; an incomplete list of log writers; lock-staleness divergence in the portal; and glossary and .gitattributes coverage gaps.

kept.surfaces: knowledge:log-management + prime(rules.ts) + docs/the-lock.md + docs/cli-reference.md + docs/progressive-mode.md vs code (core/fill-classify.ts, core/fill.ts)
kept.claim: The --approve log gate is ALL-OR-NOTHING: if ANY log_required node's source drifted with no fresh entry, --approve fills NOTHING (no pair on any node).
kept.evidence: knowledge log-management.ts:111 "The log gate is ALL-OR-NOTHING at `--approve`: if ANY `log_required` node's source drifted with no fresh entry, `--approve` fills NOTHING that run — no pair on any node, related or not, is verified"; rules.ts:283 same; docs/the-lock.md:135 "at `--approve`, if *any* `log_required` node is missing its entry, the run fills **nothing at all** — no pair on any node, related or not"; docs/cli-reference.md:658 and progressive-mode.md:298-301 "a fill stops and asks for that entry — whoever moved the code, and whether or not your change went near it". Code: core/fill-classify.ts:232-236 "// The log gate's set: every component owning an unverified pair ... for (const p of unverifiedPairs) nodeSet.add(p.nodePath)"; fill.ts:411 gates only `for (const nodePath of nodeSet)`. Live ($TMPDIR/yglog-a): svc (log_required, no rules, no entry) plus other (log_required, entry, 1 script pair). `yg check --approve` printed "fill  1 pair · 1 script (free)" / "fill  done in 0s — 1 passed", and yg-lock.logs.json gained other's source + log baseline (closure). The final report still showed error[log-entry-missing] at svc.
kept.truth: The fill-time gate only considers components that own at least one unverified pair. A log_required component that owes an entry but has no pending pair (no effective rules, draft-only rules, or a change outside every rule's scope) does not stop the fill. Every other pair is filled and other nodes close, and only the final read-only re-check reports log-entry-missing.
kept.fix: Reword all five surfaces: the fill stops before recording anything when a component that has pairs waiting to be filled owes an entry. A component with no pending pairs does not stop the run but keeps the final `yg check` red via log-entry-missing. Alternatively, widen nodeSet to every log_required node if all-or-nothing is the intended contract.

kept.claim: After a merge, the recipe is: resolve lock → `yg log merge-resolve` → `git add`/commit → `yg check` / `yg check --approve`, which reconciles the log.
kept.evidence: knowledge log-management: "When BOTH `log.md` and `yg-lock.logs.json` conflicted, the order is: resolve the lock ... → `yg log merge-resolve --node <path>` per conflicted log → `yg check --approve`"; the-lock.md:139 "records the node's baseline. ... Then stage the log and `yg-lock.logs.json` and commit the merge"; CLI output "next: git add .yggdrasil/model/svc/log.md .yggdrasil/yg-lock.logs.json / then: git commit, then yg check". Code: recordBaseline sets only `entry.log = computeLogBaselineFromContent(...)` (log-merge-resolve.ts:375-377) and never touches `source`. Live ($TMPDIR/yglog-m): A and B each edited src/svc and added an entry, closing on their branch. After merge, `git checkout --ours` lock, `yg log merge-resolve --node svc` ("Log baseline updated."), then commit, `yg check` gave "error[log-entry-missing] 1 node changed with no log entry at: svc", and `yg check --approve` stayed FAIL with the same error. The state just before merge-resolve (the union with the ours lock) was only a log-cycle-open warning. The same error appears after taking --theirs (t23).
kept.truth: merge-resolve moves the log baseline to the newest entry but leaves the kept side's source fingerprint. The merged source matches neither side's fingerprint, so every log_required node whose source both branches changed owes a brand-new entry after a correctly followed merge recipe. The recipe as documented ends red.
kept.fix: Document that after merging a log_required node, a new entry is owed (ask the user for the merge's reason, per prime), and include `yg log add` in the recipe. Alternatively, have merge-resolve leave the baseline at the kept side's value (or clear `source`) so that the union's newer entry counts as fresh.

results.summary:
I audited the agent-facing surfaces of Yggdrasil 6.1.0 (release/6.1.0 at 65bfb3967, live CLI 6.1.0) against the source and against live runs in scratch projects $TMPDIR/agentsurf-p1..p14 inside the container. Surfaces covered: `yg prime` (all 501 lines), the `yg prime --digest` block and the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / .clinerules installation with its staleness gate, all 16 knowledge topics (read in full or scanned by grep), `--help` for every command and subcommand, the docs cli-reference, platforms, glossary, getting-started, configuration and the-lock pages, README, and the CHANGELOG [6.1.0] Breaking/Upgrading sections. Commands run live: init (fresh, re-run, --upgrade, --provider, --no-*, --platform, legacy sweep, subdirectory), context, tree, owner, find, impact (all 5 modes), structure, type-suggest, simulate, portal (static, served, Host check), advise, incident, suppressions, log merge-resolve during a rebase, and the flag-combination refusals.

Things that hold:
- The digest block and anchor match between the CLI, the repo's own files and the examples.
- `--upgrade` tops up .gitignore and .gitattributes, lists unknown config keys, and sweeps legacy per-platform files.
- The portal refuses a foreign Host.
- merge-resolve now works during a rebase.
- `yg verdict` is hidden and exits 1.
- The refused flag combinations (--approve with --no-approve, --top 0, --summary with --approve) are refused.
- A scripted scan of every `yg <cmd> --flag` mention on every surface found no nonexistent flag outside the help examples.

Mismatches found: 35, listed below.

The most serious:
1. Prime, the log-management topic and the-lock page all say one missing log entry on any log_required node makes `--approve` fill nothing. In the code the gate only covers nodes that own an unverified pair; a live run filled pairs anyway.
2. Prime still says a single-line yg-suppress marker waives only the line below it. That is stale since 6.1.0: a marker written after code waives its own line.
3. `yg context` refuses to assemble context over a `config-unknown-key` error, even one in the local yg-secrets.yaml, and wrongly says the graph is unreadable.
4. The help examples `yg incident list` and `yg simulate .yggdrasil/aspects/no-todo` both fail when run.
5. "Every command that takes a node answers node-not-found" is false: simulate replays a nonexistent node and exits 0, and aspect-test and tree --root word the error differently.
6. The rule-hash formula in the verification-and-lock topic, and prime's list of verdict inputs, leave out the helper files that are hashed since 6.1.0.
7. The `--dry-run` "per-node/per-aspect breakdown" wording in help, prime and knowledge no longer matches the per-pair output.
8. init prints "nothing changed" after writing `rules_artifacts` into the config.
9. docs/cli-reference contradicts itself on whether configuring a reviewer drops config comments; they are kept.

kept.surfaces: prime (templates/rules.ts:283) + knowledge:log-management (log-management.ts:111) + docs/the-lock.md:135 vs code core/fill.ts + core/fill-classify.ts
kept.claim: The log gate at --approve is all-or-nothing over ANY log_required node: one drifted node with no fresh entry means nothing is filled on any node.
kept.evidence: prime: "the log gate is ALL-OR-NOTHING at `--approve` — if ANY `log_required` node's source drifted with no fresh entry, `--approve` fills NOTHING that run (no pair on any node is verified)". the-lock.md:135: "at `--approve`, if *any* `log_required` node is missing its entry, the run fills **nothing at all** — no pair on any node, related or not." Code fill-classify.ts:232-236: "// The log gate's set: every component owning an unverified pair, unfiltered. const nodeSet ... for (const p of unverifiedPairs) nodeSet.add(p.nodePath)"; fill.ts:411 iterates only nodeSet.
